core.title: Give every user/system flow both a registry entry and a spec file
core.given: The plan tree holds a user/system flow registry grouped by theme category, and a user/system flow spec location holding one spec file per user/system flow (both placed by the profile).
core.when: You add, change, rename, regroup, remove or validate any user/system flow, registry entry or user/system flow spec file.
core.then: Ensure every user/system flow has both a registry entry in the user/system flow registry and a full spec file, named from the user/system flow's id, at the profile-defined spec location, so every registry entry has its matching spec file.
prefer: Two-file pattern per user/system flow: a summary registry entry (user/system flow identifier, description, path, product capabilities summary) plus a spec file holding the full workflow.
Create the spec file in the same change as the registry entry, named from the user/system flow's id.
Place each registry entry under its theme-category group: nominal, error, alternate or exception.
avoid: A registry entry without its spec file, including a stale entry left after the spec file is renamed or deleted.
A user/system flow spec file with no registry entry.
Spec file names that do not match the registry entry's user/system flow id.
core.why: Each user/system flow needs both files; the planner phase gate fails when a spec file is missing.
evidence: For each user/system flow id in the registry, its spec file exists at the profile-defined location, and each user/system flow spec file has a registry entry.
The registry-spec pairing check passes; the planner phase gate fails if any spec file is missing.
Every registry entry sits under one of the theme-category groups nominal, error, alternate, exception.
verification: Strict disposition, severity 3: a registry entry without its spec file fails the planner phase gate.

The check enumerates every entry in the user/system flow registry and fails for each entry whose spec file is missing; the registry index location, the per-train spec location and the spec naming come from the profile. The planner phase gate is where the rule is enforced, not a limit on the invariant, which holds for every user/system flow at all times, including pre-existing user/system flows under whole-repo validation.

Registry-entry content: the entry is the summary — user/system flow identifier, description, path, product capabilities summary — while the spec file holds the full workflow; these fields are planning-data concepts of the two-file pattern, not stack mechanics, so they stay in the core.

Grouping retention: until a separate theme-category grouping convention (proposed planner.user-system-flow.registry-grouping) is active, this rule's activation also covers grouping changes and misgrouped entries, and its doesNotFire cases require valid grouping as well as valid pairing; the theme categories are nominal, error, alternate, exception.

Validator and finding ids and the term id of the two-file pattern are realization details carried by the stack realization delivered as the worked reference example; this core names the check generically.

values: user/system flow registry entry added, renamed, removed, moved or edited
registry theme-category group added, renamed, removed or reordered
user/system flow spec file added, renamed, deleted or edited
registry entry outside a nominal/error/alternate/exception group

fires: A new user/system flow entry is added to the user/system flow registry.
A user/system flow id is renamed in the registry, or an existing user/system flow entry's contents are updated.
A registry entry is moved between theme-category groups, or a group in the registry is added, renamed, removed or reordered.
A user/system flow spec file is created, renamed, deleted or edited.
A user/system flow spec file exists with no corresponding registry entry.
Validating or reviewing existing user/system flows, including pre-existing registry entries whose spec file is missing or that sit outside a nominal/error/alternate/exception group.
doesNotFire: Planning work that touches only other plan artifacts (product capabilities, features, acceptances) and leaves the user/system flow registry and user/system flow spec files untouched, while every existing user/system flow already has a registry entry in a valid theme-category group and a matching spec file.
Source or test changes that modify no plan artifacts, while the user/system flow registry is correctly theme-category-grouped and every registry entry is paired with its spec file.

neutralityNotes: Theme-category names (nominal, error, alternate, exception), the planner phase, and the user/system flow registry / user/system flow spec artifact concepts are ATDD-methodology content and stay in the core; they are not stack mechanics. The registry-entry field concepts (user/system flow identifier, description, path, product capabilities summary) are likewise kept in the core (prefer[0] and verification) as planning-data that applies to any stack with these roles; their concrete spellings belong to the ATDD planning data model and do not vary by stack, so no profile key is proposed for them. What genuinely varies by stack is the physical placement: the registry index path (proposed key layout.registries#user_system_flow_registry, since no existing key names an enumerating index file) and the per-train spec path, which uses the existing key layout.plan_item (its doc names the path of one plan artifact under the plan root; a DESIRED OUTCOME is only an example), plus the plan-artifact suffix. The validator id SPEC-USER_SYSTEM_FLOW-VAL-0003 and the term two_file_pattern are realization details carried as bunOnly. Severity 3 and the strict disposition are rule-level and kept in core:verification, not in the profile. If a future stack needs distinct per-kind plan-item layouts at once, the vocabulary owner may revisit layout.plan_item; per the owner's guidance this core uses the single existing key.
